 Jayson Tatum (rest) is off the injury report for Friday’s matchup with the Hornets. 
 Tatum played both legs of a Sunday-Monday back-to-back set and got Wednesday off for rest. He’ll be back in action after that maintenance night and should handle his usual workload.

 Jayson Tatum (rest) has been ruled out against the Bucks on Wednesday. 
 Tatum will get the night off after playing on both Sunday and Monday. He hasn’t shot the ball particularly well, so a rest night could do him some good. Paul George will be back after missing Monday’s game, so the rest of the starting unit should remain the same, with George filling in for Tatum.

 Jayson Tatum (rest) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Tatum played both games of the Celtics’ recent back-to-back, logging 32 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Rockets. Paul George is off the injury report after not playing in Houston, so he can slide into Tatum’s spot if JT doesn’t play. 
 Jayson Tatum

 Jayson Tatum accounted for 19 points (5-of-16 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, nine assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 With Paul George out, the Rockets focused even more of their defensive attention on Tatum on Monday. While he finished one assist shy of a double-double, the Celtics star committed five turnovers and shot 1-of-7 from beyond the arc. Tatum’s fantasy value has been elite through Boston’s first seven games, so managers don’t need to worry about his performance against the Rockets. 
 Jayson Tatum

 Forward-Guard 
 #0 
 Jayson Tatum finished Sunday’s win over the Magic with 32 points (8-of-19 FGs, 15-of-17 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, two blocks and one three-pointer. 
 Tatum didn’t have his best day shooting the basketball, but his ability to get to the foul line paid off immensely. He made 15 of his 17 free-throw attempts, the second time in three games that the Celtics’ forward has scored at least 15 points on free throws. Add in the assists and blocks, and this was a solid end to the week for those rostering Tatum. Boston plays four games next week, starting with the Rockets on Monday.

 Hugo González has replaced Jordan Walsh in the starting lineup for Sunday’s game against the Magic. 
 The Celtics’ initial starting lineup had just one replacement: Neemias Queta for Mitchell Robinson (rest). However, González has replaced Walsh, who will be available off the bench. Derrick White, Paul George and Jayson Tatum complete the starting lineup. 
 Jayson Tatum

 Jayson Tatum amassed 26 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Tatum has scored 23 points or more in each of his last four games, rebounding well after a quiet outing in Boston’s season opener. Against the Bulls, he scored 16 of his 26 points in the first half, shooting 7-of-11 from the field. Tatum cooled off after halftime, but it didn’t matter much as Boston had already built up a large lead. He’ll look to finish the week on a high when the Celtics face the Magic on Sunday. 
 Jordan Walsh 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Jordan Walsh produced 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Nets. 
 In Boston’s first three games, Walsh shot 4-of-12 from the field and scored nine points. He matched that total in the first half of Tuesday’s overtime win, and his 15 points are his most in a game since February 11 (16 vs. Chicago). The Celtics don’t look to him for much scoring, but there can be catch-and-shoot opportunities playing off of Jayson Tatum, Paul George and Derrick White. He took advantage against the Nets, shooting 3-of-5 from deep.

 Jayson Tatum accounted for 40 points (10-of-20 FGs, 18-of-22 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Nets. 
 The Celtics’ second game in as many nights was more dramatic than many expected, as they needed overtime and a Tatum pull-up at the buzzer to beat the Nets. He finished with an excellent stat line, shooting 50 percent from the field and committing no turnovers. Counting the postseason, this was Tatum’s first 40-point game since Game 4 of the Celtics’ 2025 second-round series against the Knicks (the game in which he was injured). 
 Jayson Tatum

 Jayson Tatum lit up the Bulls with 23 points (7-of-17 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists, one steal and two three-pointers on Monday. 
 After dropping 36 points on Friday, Tatum’s scoring dipped a bit in this game. It was a slightly subpar shooting night, but he also didn’t need to score as much. Boston led by 30 points at the end of the third quarter, and the lineup that dominated the third quarter didn’t include Tatum, so he only played 28 minutes. They’ll take on the Nets on Tuesday, which will be the second night of this back-to-back. Tatum should be in for a better outing.
